title: Commutator support from equivariant ordered root coordinates
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring and $(G,T=D_A(M),\Phi,\Phi^\vee,\Delta,(X_\alpha))$ a pinned split realization [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. For each $c\in\Phi$, suppose given a group homomorphism which is a closed immersion $p_c:\mathbf G_{a,A}\to G$ whose differential identifies $A$ with $\mathfrak g_c$, and which satisfies $t p_c(z)t^{-1}=p_c(c(t)z)$ on all algebra points. Here $\mathbf G_{a,A}=\operatorname{Spec}A[z]$ with addition, and write $U_c$ for the image of $p_c$. Let $\Sigma=\{c\in\Phi:\lambda(c)>0\}$ for a homomorphism $\lambda:M\to\mathbf Z$ nonzero on every root. Assume that, for every enumeration of $\Sigma$, multiplication $\prod_{c\in\Sigma}U_c\to G$ is an isomorphism onto the same subgroup $U_\Sigma$. For distinct $a,b\in\Sigma$, put $I_{a,b}=\{(i,j)\in\mathbf Z_{>0}^2:ia+jb\in\Phi\}$. For every enumeration of $I_{a,b}$ there are coefficients $C_{i,j}\in A$ such that for every commutative $A$-algebra $R$ and $x,y\in R$,
$$p_a(x)p_b(y)p_a(-x)p_b(-y)=\prod_{(i,j)\in I_{a,b}}p_{ia+jb}(C_{i,j}x^iy^j),$$
with that enumeration on the right and coefficients mapped to $R$. In particular the two root subgroups commute if $I_{a,b}=\varnothing$. No invertibility of any integer, reducedness, connectedness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $A$.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.14 and its proof, printed pp.145--146; the positive-system coordinate hypothesis is the output of Theorem 5.1.13 used in that proof. Read online; WANTED archival literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this root-system/group-scheme result.

proof.text: The reduced-root condition in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization] gives $\mathbf Q a\cap\Phi=\{a,-a\}$. Since $a\ne b$ and $\lambda(a),\lambda(b)>0$, the roots $a,b$ are linearly independent over $\mathbf Q$. Thus $(i,j)\mapsto ia+jb$ is injective and $I_{a,b}$ is finite, being injected into the finite set $\Phi$. Every such root lies in $\Sigma$, since $\lambda(ia+jb)=i\lambda(a)+j\lambda(b)>0$. Fix the requested enumeration of $I_{a,b}$ and extend its root enumeration to an enumeration of $\Sigma$.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.14, proof, printed pp.145--146; the ordered positive-root coordinate isomorphism of Theorem 5.1.13 is assumed in the item. Universal-algebra version of the coefficient argument, written by Q87.

proof.text: Each closed immersion $p_c$ identifies $\mathbf G_{a,A}$ with its image $U_c$: the affine description of a closed immersion in [def-weil-closed-immersion] is a quotient of coordinate rings, and [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies its source with that closed subscheme. Hence the assumed multiplication isomorphism gives bijections $q_R:R^\Sigma\to U_\Sigma(R)$, $q_R((z_c))=\prod_c p_c(z_c)$, natural in every $A$-algebra $R$, in the chosen order. Set $B=A[X,Y]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $K=p_a(X)p_b(Y)p_a(-X)p_b(-Y)\in U_\Sigma(B)$. This membership uses precisely the subgroup hypothesis. Define $h_c\in B$ by $q_B((h_c))=K$. For $X\mapsto x,Y\mapsto y$ in any $A$-algebra $R$, naturality and uniqueness give $q_R((h_c(x,y)))=p_a(x)p_b(y)p_a(-x)p_b(-y)$.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.14, proof, printed pp.145--146; the ordered positive-root coordinate isomorphism of Theorem 5.1.13 is assumed in the item. Universal-algebra version of the coefficient argument, written by Q87.

proof.text: Conjugation distributes across an ordered product, and the assumed equivariance of each $p_c$ gives $tq_R((z_c))t^{-1}=q_R((c(t)z_c))$. Applying this also to the four factors of the commutator, uniqueness of the $q_R$ coordinates gives $h_c(a(t)x,b(t)y)=c(t)h_c(x,y)$ for all $R,t,x,y$. In particular take $R=A[M][X,Y]$ and the point $t\in D_A(M)(R)$ induced by the coefficient inclusion $A[M]\to R$ [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Under $T\simeq D_A(M)$ and $T\subseteq G$, a point of $T(R)$ is an $A$-algebra map $A[M]\to R$ lying in $G(R)$, and its character value $m(t)$ is the image of $e_m$ [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Then $m(t)=e_m$ and the identity is the polynomial identity $h_c(e_aX,e_bY)=e_c h_c(X,Y)$ in $A[M][X,Y]$.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.14, proof, printed pp.145--146; the ordered positive-root coordinate isomorphism of Theorem 5.1.13 is assumed in the item. Universal-algebra version of the coefficient argument, written by Q87.

proof.text: Since each $p_c$ is a group homomorphism, $p_c(0)=1$ and $p_c(-z)=p_c(z)^{-1}$. Evaluating the universal commutator at $Y=0$ or $X=0$ therefore gives the identity. Its unique $q$ coordinates are all zero, so $h_c(X,0)=0$ in $A[X]$ and $h_c(0,Y)=0$ in $A[Y]$. Write $h_c=\sum_{i,j\ge0}d_{c,i,j}X^iY^j$, with finitely many nonzero coefficients [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Coefficient comparison in these two evaluations gives $d_{c,i,0}=d_{c,0,j}=0$ for all $i,j\ge0$.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.14, proof, printed pp.145--146; the ordered positive-root coordinate isomorphism of Theorem 5.1.13 is assumed in the item. Universal-algebra version of the coefficient argument, written by Q87.

proof.text: Compare the coefficient of $X^iY^j$ in the identity of step 3, using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $e_ae_b=e_{a+b}$ from [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. It gives $d_{c,i,j}e_{ia+jb}=d_{c,i,j}e_c$ in $A[M]$. If $ia+jb\ne c$, the coefficient of the basis vector $e_{ia+jb}$ is $d_{c,i,j}$ on the left and zero on the right. Hence $d_{c,i,j}=0$ in $A$. This uses the specified free $A$-basis of the group algebra and requires neither cancellation of a scalar nor testing at field-valued points.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.14, proof, printed pp.145--146; the ordered positive-root coordinate isomorphism of Theorem 5.1.13 is assumed in the item. Universal-algebra version of the coefficient argument, written by Q87.

proof.text: By steps 4--5, only coefficients with $i,j>0$ and $c=ia+jb$ can survive. The independence proved in step 1 makes this pair unique for each $c$ [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Thus $h_{ia+jb}=C_{i,j}X^iY^j$ with $C_{i,j}=d_{ia+jb,i,j}\in A$, and all other $h_c$ vanish. Insert these coordinates into the universal product in step 2 and delete the factors $p_c(0)=1$. The remaining factors have the originally requested order. Evaluation $A[X,Y]\to R$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] gives exactly the asserted identity for every $R,x,y$. If $I_{a,b}$ is empty the product is $1$, so $p_a(x)p_b(y)=p_b(y)p_a(x)$ for all such points. The chosen enumeration was arbitrary.
